Maya (PM): Heads up — ACME pilot asked for exact parity on per-tenant routing + per-route SLOs. We need to decide whether to pursue full parity or scope a lightweight shim for the pilot.
Omar (Eng): Quick Q — what's the rough delta to ship full parity vs a shim?
Maya (PM): Short answer: parity ~= routing filters + config APIs + persistence + UI = ~3 sprints eng + infra work. Shim = routing rules + traffic shaping + limited config surface, but technical debt.
Raj (Sales): From my calls: ACME will sign Dedicated if we deliver parity. If we offer a pilot-only compromise, they'll ask for discount/credits. This is real deal revenue.
Priya (SRE/SE): Technically a "shim" could be an adapter that implements expected routing semantics on top of current runtime, but we'll need robust metrics and alerting. I'm thinking ~4w work to be safe.
Ben (Design): Adapter will still need a settings surface for tenant admins. Low-fi is fine for pilot (toggles + basic explanations).
Lina (Head of Product): We can't slip the GA by 3 sprints. Propose two options to the execs: Option 1 — Pilot adapter (4w) + pilot-only SLA; Option 2 — Full parity (12w) and go for enterprise commit. Decision needed by EOW.
Omar (Eng): Minor correction — adapter + metrics + rollout automation is closer to 4w dev + 1w infra testing, not 2w. Also requires a canary plan.
Maya (PM): OK update: Option A = adapter + canary rollout (~4w) + pilot SLA; Option B = full parity (~12w) for GA. Trade-offs: speed vs long-term maintenance.
Raj (Sales): Sales can accept Option A if we lock pilot-only SLA and price for risk. We can push ACME to sign pilot in Q2 and close GA decision by mid-Q3.
Lina (Head of Product): To approve Option A we need a checklist. Draft launch criteria: 
```
- pilot SLA doc signed
- runtime per-tenant routing rules available (adapter)
- observability: per-tenant latency/cost/time-series
- alerting on SLO breaches + incident playbook
- customer acceptance test (integration & perf)
```
If we choose full parity, add: config REST APIs, policy UI, audit logs, multi-tenant persistence model.
Priya (SRE/SE): Also recommend fallback policy: default to a lighter model variant / degrade gracefully when SLOs are under pressure. That reduces infra burn and keeps customer UX stable. Adds ~2w if we build it now.
Omar (Eng): Fallback logic is reasonable as an opt-in for pilot. We can scope it as engineering toggle to avoid product churn.
doc-bot: New doc created — https://docs.redwood.internal/PRD/2812345678 (Maya: PRD skeleton) :memo:
Maya (PM): Recap + asks: product approve Option A (adapter, 4w + opt-in fallback) and sales commit to pilot-only SLA + pricing. Engineering to deliver tech design doc by Tue.
Lina (Head of Product): Approve Option A with conditions: (1) Tech design by Tue, (2) Product to own metrics/kpis and midpoint GA decision, (3) Engineering to estimate fallback effort in that doc.
Ben (Design): I'll put together a quick mock of the tenant settings panel and can share Figma link by Wed.
Raj (Sales): I'll update ACME SOW to reflect pilot-only SLA and pricing concessions; collateral ready by Thu.
Priya (SRE/SE): I'll draft acceptance tests and monitoring checklist and attach to the PRD.
Maya (PM): Thanks everyone — I'll file follow-ups (PRD, action items) and set a short sync Mon to confirm scope.
